translationRepairs: In a secret memorial he reported that because Yixin had the Crown Prince administer state affairs, Yixin was ill at ease, met often with Zhang Xiaojie, and he feared there was a covert plot to shake the Crown Prince.

In a secret memorial he reported that because the Crown Prince administered state affairs, Yixin was ill at ease, met often with Zhang Xiaojie, and he feared there was a covert plot to shake the Crown Prince.

密奏乙辛以皇太子知國政，心不自安 treats 以皇太子知國政 as the circumstance that made Yixin uneasy: the Crown Prince administered state affairs. The old literal wrongly makes Yixin the agent who had the prince do so; the proposed wording restores the correct agency.
The emperor took the point and posted Yixin as military commissioner at Zhongjing.
The emperor took the point and posted Yixin as regent (liushou) of Zhongjing.
出乙辛為中京留守 names the office 留守 (capital regent/liushou), not 節度使. Calling him military commissioner is a title error; the proposed regent (liushou) matches the Chinese office.
On Yixin's birthday the emperor sent the courtier Yelu Aisiben with gifts; Yixin asked him privately to tell the throne, "I see villains at court and Your Majesty isolated in danger.
On Yixin's birthday the emperor sent the courtier Yelu Baisiben with gifts; Yixin asked him privately to tell the throne, "I see villains at court and Your Majesty isolated in danger.
近臣耶律白斯本 begins with 白 (Bai); the given name is Baisiben, not Aisiben. The replacement corrects the mistransliteration without other change.
When Aisiben returned he reported this to the emperor.
When Baisiben returned he reported this to the emperor.
白斯本還 names the same courtier as 白斯本 (Baisiben). Aisiben is unsupported by the Chinese characters.
Yelu Sala, styled Jinyin, was grandson of the Southern Chancellery King's Molugu.
Yelu Sala, styled Jinyin, was grandson of Molugu, the Southern Chancellery King.

南院大王磨魯古之孫 is apposition: Molugu, who was Southern Chancellery King. "the Southern Chancellery King's Molugu" wrongly reads as possession; the proposed apposition matches the Chinese order of title then name.
In the second year of Dakang, with Yelu Yixin at Zhongjing, the court deliberated recalling him—yet none of the ministers dared speak plainly.
In the second year of Dakang, with Yelu Yixin as regent of Zhongjing, the court deliberated recalling him—yet none of the ministers dared speak plainly.
耶律乙辛為中京留守 states that Yixin held the Zhongjing liushou post. "at Zhongjing" omits the office 為…留守; "as regent of Zhongjing" restores that explicit appointment.
If the late emperor had accepted the charges against Empress Shunsheng, Yixin would count as a meritorious minister—how then could Your Majesty have ascended the throne?
If the late emperor had believed the accusations against your late father, Yixin would count as a meritorious minister—how then could Your Majesty have ascended the throne?

The Siku Liao Shi and the imperial biography identify 順考 as Emperor Tianzuo's deceased father, Crown Prince Yelu Jun, posthumously Emperor Daxiao Shunsheng and Shunzong. The sentence concerns accusations against the prince, not an empress or a person named Shunkao.
